Scope: collector and local roads, potable water, sewerage, storm drainage, irrigation, medium-voltage, street lighting and telecom networks, a sewage pump station and storm drainage ponds for Block J. Contract value 117.4M SAR excluding VAT, 24 months.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted effort (now stated in man-hours: 523,360 in total, the same budget as the 65,420 man-days of report 96). At the 17-Nov-2026 data date the project is 80.1% complete against 89.5% planned, behind by 9.4% (SPI 0.90). Since report 96 it gained 0.48% against 1.03% planned, so the gap widened from 8.8%; finishing on the contract date would need 2.84% a week.

Data notes

Built from the W08 upload (report 97, with a separate Risk Log, Issue Log and RI-Register); the previous week's folder (report 96) was used for this-week changes.

  • The milestone sheet again states the contract week ("Current Contract Weeks: 96 of 104"), which matches 674 days from handover on 12-Jan-2025 to the 17-Nov-2026 data date, so this is week 96.
  • The workbook was rebuilt in a new layout this week: effort is now in man-hours (523,360, equal to report 96's 65,420 man-days × 8) and the networks are grouped under four work packages with unchanged weights.
  • Planned to date differs between sheets: 89.47% in the Progress sheet and cover, 89.63% in the Physical-Chart Data Weekly sheet. This week's plan is 3,072 man-hours (0.59%) in the Progress sheet but 5,396 (1.03%) in the chart data; the cumulative plan rose 1.05% from report 96's 88.42%.
  • The chart data was restated: baseline and revised plan columns are identical, and the earned effort is exactly 3,256 man-hours (0.62%) in each of the five weeks from 13-Oct to 10-Nov-2026, which looks filled in rather than measured.
  • The weekly activities sheet repeats all seven lines of report 96 word for word. The summary sheet adds 180 LM of storm drainage and 47 LM of potable water, but the Progress sheet earns nothing on those networks this week; street lighting adds 1,000 LM and 1,480 man-hours.
  • The Major Quantities sheet appears to be calculated from percentages rather than measured (every sewer line shows the same +0.82% variance and every storm main line 100%). It shows all 18,200 m of kerb installed while no curbstone has been delivered (0 of 42,552 pieces).
  • The Testing sheet now shows testing under way since June to November 2026 (54.9% overall, forecast to finish by 09-Sep-2027), whereas report 96 showed none started. Testing and commissioning is 72.4% earned against 4.6% planned in the Progress sheet.
  • Invoice 21 (01 to 15-Oct-2026, submitted 15-Oct) appears for the first time, and invoice 20 is now shown as paid on 13-Oct-2026, although report 96 listed it as awaiting payment.
  • Manpower: the trade table plans 112 manual workers but the Manpower sheet's weekly row plans 129.5; equipment is planned at 91 on the cover and 106.9 in the Manpower sheet. The cover's required level of 400 workers is far above either plan.
  • The separate Risk Log and Issue Log are identical to report 96's sheets. The RI-Register's dashboard (3 open risks, 4 open issues) does not match its own logs (2 open risks, 2 open issues), and its notes refer to ISS-07 and ISS-09, which are not in the log. The cover's first top issue measures slippage with cost-based progress.
  • Failed starts on the cover read 509 last week and 493 this week, but report 96's cover showed 429. Activity counts differ: 1,268 completed and 540 not started in the P6 file, 1,262 and 546 in the Schedule sheet.
  • The P6 project ID changed again, to MOD3-J-2769-BL01-R01-5 (R01-4 last week). In one week it moved the network milestones 5 to 45 days earlier while physical progress rose 0.48%; no revised logic or recovery schedule approval is recorded.
  • The HSE inspection sheet still covers 26-Aug to 01-Sep-2026 yet gives this week's safety score (0.95); the consultant inspection log ends on 27-Oct-2026. The summary sheet still gives site handover as 12-Feb-2025, and the procurement log keeps over-deliveries and the unit typos "m132" and "m133".
  • Several cover fields show #REF! (EAC), and the invoice log still has stray values of 21,100,000, 20,900,000 and 200,000.
  • Photos: 13 new photos were uploaded, none repeating earlier weeks; six are used. Six of the new photos carry camera date stamps (10 to 17-Nov-2026).
